## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `retrieval-action-ranking`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-08-16T10:35:34.761Z.

Signal candidate (45) — retrieval-action ranking: score the next *call* by declared cost against expected information, not only the next *item* by relevance. Measured 2026-08-16.

Candidates (39) through (44) all answer variants of one question: given a candidate set of items, how should they be scored, cut, or re-denominated. Every one of them operates after retrieval has already happened. This candidate is the first in the catalogue that operates before it, and it is proposed because the cost side of the ratio is already declared and nothing reads it.

## The measurement that forces it

`pm contracts --summary --json` publishes, for every command, `default_max_estimated_tokens` and `default_max_estimated_tokens_by_format`. That is a declared upper bound on what a call will cost, available for the price of one 2.6k-token read, before any of the calls are made.

Measured actual costs on this workspace, against the surfaces an agent uses to orient:

  call                                    tokens
  pm guide <topic> --depth brief             640
  pm list-open --limit 20                    909
  pm context --limit 10                    2,063
  pm next                                  2,525
  pm contracts --summary                   2,637
  pm help                                  3,136
  pm contracts --command list --flags-only 3,372
  pm guide commands --depth standard       7,981

And the documents those surfaces route into:

  docs/DEPENDENCY_KIND_CONTRACT.md           692
  docs/SCRIPTING.md                        1,933
  docs/READ_OUTPUT_CONTRACTS.md            3,590
  docs/MERGE_SAFETY.md                     4,443
  docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md                      5,560
  docs/RELATIONSHIP_GRAPH.md               7,393
  docs/COMMANDS.md                        28,980
  docs/SDK.md                             45,117

The spread is two orders of magnitude, and until this session none of it was declared to the agent making the choice. Every routing surface in the project — AGENTS.md, the guide topics, all twelve skill bundles — presented `docs/SDK.md` and `docs/DEPENDENCY_KIND_CONTRACT.md` as equally weighted links. An agent following the cheaper-looking route could pay sixty-five times more for it.

That is a ranking problem, and it is exactly the problem this engine exists to solve, applied one layer earlier than the engine currently reaches.

## The candidate, stated generally

Treat a retrieval action as a scored candidate. For an action `a` answering a question `q`:

  value(a, q) = expected_information(a, q) / declared_cost(a)

where `declared_cost` comes from the contract rather than from having paid it, and `expected_information` is estimated from signals the engine already computes: overlap between the question's terms and the action's declared `intent`, whether the action's output type matches the question's shape, and whether the caller has already served the same content this session.

Three properties make this tractable here and not elsewhere.

The cost is declared, not learned. Most retrieval-ranking work has to estimate cost by sampling. Here the ceiling is contract data, generated from the same table that drives help and completions, so it is exact, free, and already gated against drift. A signal whose denominator is free is rare.

The action set is small and enumerated. Seventy-five commands, twelve guide topics, fifty-six documents. This is a bounded ranking problem at every workspace size, which is the property that lets it serve both ends of the declared range — the three-item scratch project and the million-item corpus rank the same action set, because the action set is a property of the product, not of the corpus.

Redundancy is measurable across calls. The session ledger already records which items a read served. Extending it to record which *actions* were taken makes the diversity term in candidate (43) apply across calls, not only within one result: the second call that would return mostly what the first returned scores near zero without anyone declaring it redundant.

## Why this belongs to the context engine

The engine's stated job is to assemble the best context under a token budget. Today it interprets that as choosing rows within one call. But an agent's budget is spent across calls, and the largest single decision it makes is which call to issue. A relevance engine that ranks perfectly inside a 4,000-token read, while the agent has just spent 45,000 tokens reading the wrong document, has optimised the smaller term.

This also composes with what is already catalogued rather than competing with it. Candidate (42)'s dispersion gate applies unchanged: an action whose expected information is flat across the plausible questions contributes nothing and is skipped. Candidate (43)'s coverage-preserving selection is the within-call analogue of the across-call diversity term above. Candidate (44)'s event-quantile recency supplies the "have I already seen this" input without a wall-clock constant.

## Degeneracy clauses, mandatory for entry in this catalogue

On a workspace with three items, most reads fall far below their declared ceilings, so the cost term is near-uniform and the ranking reduces to expected information alone — which is the correct behaviour for `pm-z436` and needs no special path.

On a workspace where every read is truncated, the cost term saturates at the ceiling for every action, and the ranking again reduces to expected information — correct, because at that point the differentiator genuinely is what the call returns, not what it costs.

With one action available the ranking is trivially that action. It never refuses and never errors.

It cannot admit information the action set does not already contain. It reorders and skips; it does not invent a retrieval path.

## What must be measured before promotion

Whether declared ceilings track actual cost closely enough to rank with. `pm-s2h0mq` already found that ten of thirty reads exceed their own declared ceiling, one by 104x. A cost denominator that is wrong by two orders of magnitude for a third of the action set will rank worse than no cost term at all. That item is therefore a hard prerequisite, not a related concern, and this candidate must not be weighted until the declared ceilings are shown to bound the real ones.

The second measurement is whether `intent` strings carry enough signal to estimate expected information. They are one short sentence per command, written for humans. If they do not discriminate, the estimate needs a different input — most likely the command's declared output contract, which names the shape of what comes back.

Routed through `pm-g8t7b9` like every other entry in this catalogue. Candidate only. Do not weight it on the strength of this note.

Scope clarification from individual-ownership review: pm-s2h0mq owns a related measurement, read primitive or defect fix. It does not independently deliver this proposed ranking behavior. Reuse its evidence and public API; evaluate the additional behavior in this experiment.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented. Distinct objective: retrieval action ranking.

Define a versioned public-SDK input/output and parameter contract, with exact source receipts and bounded time, memory and token complexity.; Implement an isolated reproducible prototype and compare held-out quality, task success, costs, cold-start behavior and negative controls against the unchanged baseline.; Record an accept, reject, or defer decision with evidence; production implementation requires an accepted decision and its own linked delivery scope.
A falsifiable decision on retrieval action ranking with reusable benchmark evidence and no unreviewed production policy change.
